title: Wardan the Butcher; His Adventure With the Lady and the Bear

keywords: wardan the butcher; his adventure with the lady and the bear
full_text:
In Cairo lived an honest and respected butcher named Wardan who kept a flourishing stall in the meat bazaar. Every morning for a month, a wealthy, veiled lady accompanied by two servants arrived at his stall, purchased a whole fat sheep, paid with bright gold dinars without asking for change, and had the meat carried away in a wicker hamper.

Wardan was grateful for her generous custom, yet curious as to why a single household required an entire sheep each day. One morning, having packed the meat into the hamper, Wardan followed the servants at a discreet distance through winding alleys, across ancient aqueducts, until they entered a grand, isolated mansion outside the city walls.

Peering through a crack in the garden gate, Wardan beheld an extraordinary sight: the lady opened an iron trapdoor leading down into an underground vaulted cellar, where an enormous, gentle brown bear was chained to a stone pillar! The bear, which had been raised from a cub by her late father, was fed the fresh meat, while the lady tended its bedding with affectionate care.

Suddenly, two armed brigands who had scaled the back wall leaped into the courtyard, drawing their scimitars to rob the lady's mansion and seize her ancestral jewels!

Wardan did not hesitate. Drawing his heavy meat cleaver and shouting a loud battle-cry, the sturdy butcher leaped over the wall and charged the brigands with fearless valor. The bear, seeing his mistress threatened, snapped his chain with a mighty roar and joined the fray!

Terrified by the combined assault of a furious butcher and a roaring bear, the brigands threw down their weapons and begged for mercy. Wardan bound them securely with ropes and delivered them to the city magistrate.

The grateful lady rewarded Wardan with five hundred gold dinars and made his shop the exclusive supplier for her vast estates. Wardan returned to his stall with his head held high, having learned that true courage leaps to the defense of the innocent without calculating the danger.
moral: Curiosity must be balanced with prudence, and courage in uncovering truth delivers the innocent.
